To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
problematic social media usage and cyberbullying are related to each other and are associated with social connectedness and belongingness, and depression.

problematic social media usage and cyberbullying behavior were directly and positively associated with each other among high school and college students; belongingness was directly related to cyberbullying perpetuation, but indirectly related to problematic social media use; depression was a direct and significant predictor of problematic social use, and an indirect predictor, via belongingness, of cyberbullying behavior.
“Cyberbullying perpetration is strongly associated with problematic social media use, and both of these behaviors are strongly associated with belongingness and depression.”

the relationships between problematic online behaviors, psychosocial factors, and age among high school and college students.
the relationship between problematic social media and cyberbullying among adolescents and emerging adults, and the role of belongingness and social connectedness on this relationship.
the relationship between problematic social media and cyberbullying among adolescents and emerging adults, and the psychosocial factors that may contribute to these associations.
